article_text:
Art Review

Valerio Adami’s Hot and Cold Art

His syncretic style melds Pop Art’s cool, outlined forms with expressionism’s figural distortions, resulting in a perturbing ambiguity.

The Italian artist Valerio Adami, who was born in Bologna in 1935, is not as well known in America as Giorgio Morandi , Alberto Burri , and Francesco Clemente , but he should be. His exhibition Alice in the Land of Violence at David Nolan Gallery, which inaugurates the gallery’s new spacious Tribeca digs, is his first in New York in more than 20 years. All but one of the 16 paintings and 15 drawings are dated between 1962 and 1967. The exception is “Hotel Pulitzer,” which the artist completed this year at age 91, and which shows no loss of acuity.

The exhibition focuses on a body of powerful, visually innovative work done during a turbulent period when art was changing globally. In 1955, after graduating from art school in Milan and moving to Paris, Adami met Roberto Matta and Wifredo Lam . By the late ’50s, he was traveling regularly and spending time in London and New York, as well as South America and India, befriending artists, philosophers, and writers such as Richard Hamilton, Jim Dine , Oskar Kokoschka , Jacques Derrida, Édouard Glissant , and Octavio Paz.

Even though Adami’s work of the ‘60s has been associated with Pop Art, his range of inspirations and artistic dialogues extends beyond that connection and includes surrealism (Matta’s fragmented machinery and fantastical architecture and Lam’s hybrid combinations of animal and human), expressionism (Francis Bacon and Kokoschka’s distorted bodies), and Pop Art (flat saturated colors and black outlines). Rather than being overwhelmed by these diverse styles, Adami’s syncretic approach early in his career enabled him to absorb and transform these possibilities into something all his own. In contrast to his American counterparts and their love of onomatopoeia, Adami’s paintings are full of ambiguous shapes and words that resist any reductive reading.

article_text:
Hernán Goldfrid reúne a dos grandes figuras del cine argentino en una comedia de suspenso con una premisa atractiva, pero algunos problemas de desarrollo.

Ricardo Darín y Diego Peretti vuelven a compartir pantalla en Lo dejamos acá , la nueva película de Hernán Goldfrid que combina comedia negra, suspenso y un particular juego psicológico. Con estreno en Netflix previsto para el 16 de octubre, el film parte de una idea interesante y encuentra en sus protagonistas su principal fortaleza, aunque no consigue sostener todas sus posibilidades hasta el final.

La película, exhibida en el Festival de San Sebastián , marcó el regreso de Goldfrid al mundo del séptimo arte luego de más de una década. El director de Tesis sobre un homicidio vuelve a trabajar con Darín en una historia escrita por Emanuel Diez, guionista de El encargado y Nada .

¿De qué va la cinta?

Darín se mete en la piel de Ulises Verón, un prestigioso psicólogo que, cansado de los fracasos de su profesión, decide rechazar un premio a su trayectoria y cuestionar públicamente los métodos tradicionales de la terapia. Su particular forma de trabajar consiste en intervenir directamente en la vida de sus pacientes, convencido de que puede ayudarlos a resolver sus problemas de manera más efectiva .

Todo cambia con la llegada de Martín Bouchard (Peretti), un escritor exitoso que atraviesa un bloqueo creativo y depende del alcohol para encontrar inspiración. Ulises acepta el desafío de ayudarlo, pero sus métodos poco convencionales pronto convierten la relación entre ambos en un enfrentamiento de egos, manipulaciones y situaciones cada vez más inquietantes.

La dupla Darín y Peretti, es sin dudas el gran atractivo

La película encuentra sus mejores momentos en la simbiosis de ambos. Darín construye a un terapeuta convencido de tener siempre la razón, mientras que Peretti aporta los matices de un escritor que no está dispuesto a dejarse manejar fácilmente.

Reseña de “Wildwood: Bosque Salvaje”, una aventura de magia y amor familiar

La química entre ambos sostiene buena parte del relato y permite que los diálogos funcionen incluso cuando el guion no profundiza demasiado en sus personajes . También se destacan las intervenciones de Antonia Bengoechea como Paula, la hija y asistente de Ulises, y de I nés Efron dentro de la galería de pacientes.

Goldfrid acompaña estas actuaciones con una puesta en escena cuidada, especialmente en los encuentros entre el terapeuta y su paciente, donde la tensión se construye a partir de las miradas, los silencios y las intenciones ocultas.

El principal problema de Lo dejamos acá aparece cuando la historia intenta abandonar la comedia para convertirse en un thriller psicológico más oscuro. La película introduce giros y situaciones que buscan sorprender, pero no siempre consigue integrarlos de manera natural con lo que venía construyendo .

La idea de un profesional que rompe los límites de su propia disciplina ofrecía posibilidades para explorar la manipulación, la ética y las contradicciones humanas. Sin embargo, el guion prefiere avanzar hacia un juego de suspenso que, por momentos, deja de lado la profundidad de sus personajes y se vuelve vacío.

¿Vale la pena ver Lo dejamos acá?

Lo dejamos acá es una película entretenida, prochoclera, como se estila decir en el último tiempo. La mezcla entre humor negro y suspenso le permite construir momentos de tensión, aunque el desarrollo termina siendo menos sólido de lo esperado.

El resultado es una propuesta correcta para ver en Netflix , sostenida principalmente por el talento de Darín y Peretti, que deja la sensación de que podía haber llegado bastante más lejos.

Calificación: 6/10.

article_text:
“ The State of Us ,” the British coming-age-comedy starring Samuel Bottomley (“California Schemin’,” “How To Have Sex”) and Callum Scott Howells (“Madfabulous,” “It’s a Sin”), is set to land in U.K. cinemas following a deal with Vertigo Releasing .

The film, the directorial debut of Jake Harvey and Ollie Gardner, had its world premiere in the main competition at the Edinburgh International Film Festival earlier this year and will now release theatrically in the U.K. in 2027. News of Vertigo’s acquisition comes ahead of Monday’s screening of “The State of Us” at the Rome Film Festival.

Related Stories

Hulu's Mother-Son Mystery 'Phony' Mutes Connie Britton's Charisma Under Visual Effects: TV Review

The Yorkshire-shot feature is set over one unforgettable night and follows two lifelong best friends as they cling to one final chance to feel alive together. The story follows nineteen-year-old Frankie as he breaks his dying friend Taylor out of a hospice for their annual ritual: watching fireworks from their favourite hilltop, in memory of Frankie’s parents. But as their riotous night out spirals into chaos, their friendship is pushed to breaking point and Frankie finally confronts the truth he has been circling all night, revealing just how far he is willing to go to avoid being left behind. As Taylor’s time runs out, he leaves Frankie with one final wish: to find beauty in the wreckage and the will to keep living.

Popular on Variety

Alongside Bottomley and Scott Howells, the cast also includes Safia Oakley-Green (“Anemone,” “The Bluff”), Seamus O’Hara (“The Irish Goodbye,” “House of Guinness”), Sunetra Sarker (“Brookside,” “Ackley Bridge”) and Frances Barber (“Mr Holmes,” “Trick or Treat”).

Written by Harvey, the film is produced by Pippa Cross, Dylan Rees and Harvey, whose credits include “Chalet Girl,” “Made in Italy” and “7 Keys,” with original music composed by Tom Ogden, frontman of indie band Blossoms. Executive producers are James Scott and James Spring of Circus Studios together with Rachel Hunter, Alastair Mavor and Janette Day.

Circus Studios is handling worldwide sales.

“The State of Us” is presented by Noughty Pictures in association with Screen Yorkshire and produced by Restless Pictures and Crossday Productions in association with 4 8 Fourteen Films and Circus Studios. Post-production was handled by Playhouse Studios.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE : Slava Denisov’s short film The Ride is getting the feature treatment with Alex Roe ( The 5th Wave ), Jack Topalian ( Euphoria ) and Shakira Barrera ( GLOW ) on board to star.

Told entirely from the perspective of a single automobile and due to begin production in Los Angeles this fall, The Ride “follows a ‘76 Plymouth as it reflects on its journey, witnessing decades of human life, capturing moments of freedom, temptation and redemption as it changes hands from one owner to the next. A failed actress, a desperate father, two outlaws on the run – and The Ride that remembers all of them.”

Related Stories

Shakira Barrera Signs With Innovative Artists

'Ironheart': Shakira Barrera Joins Marvel Studios' Disney+ Series

The original short, narrated by Ron Perlman, premiered at the LA Shorts International Film Festival and was selected by more than 40 other festivals, earning 18 awards.

Watch on Deadline

The story was created by Denisov alongside Grigory Borodavkin who wrote the script. Andrey Valentsov will return as cinematographer, with Denisov producing alongside Daniel Shapovalov and Elena Serebryannaya of 552 Films, and Oscar-nominated screenwriter and producer Paul Tamasy ( The Fighter ). Elizaveta Menis, Roe, and Topalian join five-time Emmy-nominated Kico Velarde ( Jay Leno’s Garage ) as executive producers.

“It’s an absolute trip to watch this small experiment grow into something so much bigger,” said Denisov. “After every festival screening, people would come up and tell me about their own cars and the memories tied to them. That made me realize just how universal this idea is. Making The Ride as my first feature, with this cast and team, is truly a dream come true.”

Recently, Roe had a starring role in Amazon’s Billy the Kid as the notorious Pat Garrett opposite Tom Blyth’s Billy. Barrera is best known for her role as Yolanda aka Yo-Yo on Netflix’s GLOW .

Roe is represented by Gersh, Megan Silverman Management, and Goodman Genow; Topalian by Stewart Talent and Silver J Management; and Barrera by Innovative Artists, Brillstein Entertainment Partners, and Goodman Genow.

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "“请直接进来”：Maggie’s癌症关怀中心30周年影像展——图片报道", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一项新的摄影展纪念了Maggie’s中心成立30周年，该中心为受癌症影响的人们提供免费的实用、情感和社会支持。摄影师塔比莎·朱萨（Tabitha Jussa）的影像受“请直接进来”这一贯穿每家Maggie’s中心的精神启发，记录了这些中心内展开的充满慰藉、对话与休憩的日常瞬间", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "威勒尔（Wirral）的Maggie’s中心。塔比莎·朱萨使用固定在一个位置的大画幅相机创作了每一幅大型照片。这些照片采用胶片拍摄并通过数字分层，将一小时内记录的许多瞬间交织在一起图片来源：Tabitha Jussa", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "邓迪（Dundee）的Maggie’s中心。这些中心在平静、非机构化且欢迎访客并提供人性化氛围的建筑中，为受癌症影响的人们提供免费的实用、情感和社会支持图片来源：Tabitha Jussa", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "南安普敦（Southampton）的一家Maggie’s中心。该摄影展探讨了门槛——入口、门道和过渡空间——以及抵达Maggie’s中心的体验图片来源：Tabitha Jussa", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "奥尔德姆（Oldham）的Maggie’s中心。这些影像展示了建筑如何传达关怀与同理心，以及跨越门槛如何成为获得支持的第一步图片来源：Tabitha Jussa", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "邓迪（Dundee），选自《偶遇》（Incidental）系列。除了《在一起》（Together）系列之外，朱萨还创作了这组模拟胶片摄影作品，捕捉了每个中心更安静的细节图片来源：Tabitha Jussa", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "爱丁堡的Maggie’s中心：银盐黑白明胶摄影印相。精选的35mm胶片照片使用基于咖啡的显影剂进行冲洗，然后通过暗室手工印相——在暗室中，光线穿过底片投射到感光纸上，随后显影成实体照片图片来源：Tabitha Jussa", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "爱丁堡的Maggie’s中心：用觅得的植物创作的蓝晒图。朱萨采用19世纪的摄影工艺，收集了中心花园里的植物，将它们放置在暴露于阳光下的感光手工纸上，创作出精致的蓝色剪影图片来源：Tabitha Jussa", "translated": true}]

article_text:
‘Just come in’: 30 years of Maggie’s cancer care centres – in pictures

A new photography exhibition marks 30 years of Maggie’s centres, which offer free practical, emotional and social support to people affected by cancer. Inspired by the phrase ‘just come in’ – the ethos at the centre of every Maggie’s – photographer Tabitha Jussa’s images document the everyday moments of comfort, conversation and pause that unfold within the centres

Maggie’s centre in Wirral. Tabitha Jussa created each large photograph using a large-format camera fixed in one position. Shot on film and digitally layered, each image brings together many moments recorded over the course of an hourPhotograph: Tabitha Jussa

Maggie’s Dundee. The centres offer free practical, emotional and social support to people affected by cancer in calm, non-institutional buildings that welcome visitors and provide a humane atmospherePhotograph: Tabitha Jussa

A Maggie’s centre in Southampton. The photography display explores thresholds – entrances, doorways and transitional spaces – and the experience of arriving at Maggie’s centresPhotograph: Tabitha Jussa

Oldham Maggie’s centre. The images show how architecture can communicate care and empathy, and how crossing a threshold can be the first step towards receiving supportPhotograph: Tabitha Jussa

Dundee, from the Incidental series. Alongside the Together series, Jussa made this series of analogue film photographs capturing the quieter details of each centrePhotograph: Tabitha Jussa

Maggie’s centre in Edinburgh: silver gelatin black and white prints. Selected 35mm film photographs were developed using a coffee-based developer and then printed by hand in the darkroom, where light is projected through the negative onto light-sensitive paper before being developed into a physical printPhotograph: Tabitha Jussa

Maggie’s Edinburgh: cyanotypecreated with foraged flora. Using a 19th-century photographic process, Jussa gathered plants from centre gardens and placed them on light-sensitive handmade paper exposed to sunlight, creating delicate blue silhouettesPhotograph: Tabitha Jussa

article_text:
ザ・ハウスメAIド 服従

劇場公開日： 2026年10月23日

映画館を探す

予告編を見る

映画チケットを U-NEXTでお得にゲット PR

解説・あらすじ

「トランスフォーマー」「ミュータント・タートルズ」シリーズのミーガン・フォックスが主演を務め、美しく従順な家政婦ロボットが巻き起こす恐怖を描いたSFエロティックスリラー。 高性能なAIロボットが普及した近未来。建設現場で働くニックは、妻の入院中に子どもたちの世話や家事を任せるため、美しい女性型AIロボットを購入する。娘が「アリス」と名付けたそのロボットは料理も掃除も育児も完璧にこなし、家族の生活を支えてくれる最高の存在となるが、ある日、ニックと性的な関係をもってしまう。自意識が芽生えたアリスの存在は、やがて人類全体に脅威をもたらしていく。 ニック役で「愛は、365の日々で」のミケーレ・モローネ、妻マギー役でテレビドラマ「HEROES ヒーローズ」のマデリン・ジーマ、娘アイラ役で「ウルフマン」のマチルダ・ファースが共演。「ティル・デス」でもミーガン・フォックスと組んだS・K・デール監督がメガホンをとり、共同製作総指揮で「バイオハザード」「サイレントヒル」シリーズのビクター・ハディダが参加。

about Games, VFX and Animation）的问答环节中发表的，工业光魔动画总监哈尔·希克尔（Hal Hickel）、游击队工作室总监扬-巴特·范贝克（Jan-Bart van Beek）、派拉蒙视觉特效总监塔拉·德马科（Tara DeMarco）、Lola视觉特效总监特伦特·克劳斯（Trent Claus）以及天舞动画制作设计师诺埃尔·特里欧（Noelle 热门文章", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“可以说是，如今这几乎是同一份工作，”范贝克说。他的工作室是《地平线》系列的幕后推手，他指出了共享的渲染与动作捕捉技术以及两门行业之间的人才流动。他以虚拟制作中使用的LED环形屏（LED volume）为例，说明了游戏技术如何影响电影制作，尽管他指出，由于玩家的选择权和自主性，游戏本质上仍然有所不同。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种双向交通也在朝另一个方向运行。德马科表示，她目前在派拉蒙的项目《明天，明天，又明天》（Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow）正在借助游戏历史学家和顾问来重现1990年代和2000年代初视频游戏的外观和玩法，而不是简单地将当今的技术应用于历史题材材料。她说，该团队正在筹备一份关于像素艺术、分辨率和游戏玩法的指南。", "links": [{"text": "“Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow,”", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/news/tomorrow-tomorrow-tomorrow-daisy-edgar-jones-release-date-1236785618/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该片由西安·海德（Siân Heder）执导，黛西·埃德加-琼斯（Daisy Edgar-Jones）主演，改编自加布里埃尔·泽文（Gabrielle Zevin）关于游戏开发人员的畅销小说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "范贝克指出，《最后生还者》和《辐射》的成功证明了视频游戏知识产权向电影和电视流动的趋势日益增长。“反过来，这种情况几乎不再真正发生了，”他回忆起1990年代基于电影的游戏的激增。不过，他警告说，改编仍然充满挑战，因为许多原作的互动体验可能会丢失。", "links": [{"text": "“The Last of Us”", "url": "https://variety.com/2025/tv/tv-reviews/the-last-of-us-season-2-review-hbo-1236360381/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种融合还延伸到了工作室评估观众反应的方式上。维拉斯克斯详细透露，《战神》的开发纳入了定期Play-test（游戏测试）、面部录制、眼动追踪以及考察叙事理解度和难度的高精度调查。“我们实际上拥有眼动追踪软件，可以真正看到他们的眼睛看向哪里，”他解释说，“在某些时刻，他们是在看我们希望他们看的地方吗？”此类反馈已经成为制作流程中不可或缺的一部分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对于希克尔来说，技术的成熟并不一定能保证更好的角色表演。在讨论《曼达洛人与古古》时，他解释了工业光魔如何决定何时将古古保留为实体木偶，以及何时需要进行数字干预。“有时候，木偶感正是你想要对观众大脑产生的影响，”他说，并指出观众很欣赏该角色的“美 Muppet 式特质”，即便某些动作需要进行数字修正。", "links": [{"text": "“The Mandalorian and Grogu,”", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/news/mandalorian-and-grogu-footage-star-wars-cinemacon-1236712864/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "希克尔还描述了该制作团队如何使用虚拟现实（VR）来勘测数字环境并模拟IMAX影院内部的不同座位位置。事实证明，Apple Vision Pro在实体搭建之前判断布景规模方面特别有用。“我们能够真正理解这个空间，并知道它有多大，哪些部分将会用实景搭建，”他回忆说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对话还涉及人工智能，维拉斯克斯将当前的焦虑比作早期对计算机动画和动作捕捉将消灭传统动画工作的担忧。他认为，这两种技术最终都扩展了艺术家的能力。“你仍然需要那种富有创造力的头脑。你仍然需要一个创意团队聚在一起使用这些工具，”他说，“但如果你背后没有灵魂，这就无济于事。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "范贝克则采取了更谨慎的立场，警告人工智能可能被滥用以及盗用其他艺术家作品的风险。“人们会用它来做真正伟大的事情，也会做真正糟糕的事情，”他强调道。与此同时，希克尔将职业就业面临的不确定性与持续创作艺术的能力区分开来。“没有任何技术创新能阻止人们去创造艺术并寻找创作艺术的方法，”他辩称，并暗示未来可能会涌现出新型的动画和视觉特效公司。", "translated": true}, {"type": article_text:
James Cameron’s “Avatar” technology helped shape the look of Sony Santa Monica Studio’s “ God of War ” games, game director Bruno Velazquez revealed at View Conference in Turin on Monday during a discussion of how increasingly intertwined filmmaking and video game production have become.

Velazquez said the studio sought to present the two most recent mainline “God of War” games as uninterrupted single takes, borrowing techniques from cinema to give the virtual camera a handheld feel. “We take inspiration from films,” he said, recalling that the developers obtained one of the cameras used by Cameron on “Avatar” and brought it onto their motion-capture set to shoot scenes alongside the performers.

Related Stories

'Moon Knight' Star May Calamawy Fronts 'Night Feeds,' Opener of New Tokyo Horror Festival Yami (EXCLUSIVE)

Family Dramas Dominate Tokyo Festival’s Asian Lineup Amid 'Geopolitical Volatility'

The comments came during an “Ask Me Anything about Games, VFX and Animation” session featuring Industrial Light & Magic animation director Hal Hickel, Guerrilla Games studio director Jan-Bart van Beek, Paramount VFX supervisor Tara DeMarco, Lola Visual Effects supervisor Trent Claus and Skydance Animation production designer Noelle Triaureau. The discussion was moderated by Wieke Schrakamp.

Popular on Variety

“Arguably, it’s almost the same job these days,” said van Beek, whose studio is behind the “Horizon” franchise, pointing to shared rendering and motion-capture technology and the migration of talent between the two industries. He cited the LED volume used in virtual production as one example of game technology influencing filmmaking, although he noted that games remain fundamentally different because of player choice and agency.

The traffic also runs in the other direction. DeMarco said her current Paramount project, “Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow,” is drawing on gaming historians and consultants to recreate the look and play of video games from the 1990s and early 2000s, rather than simply applying present-day technology to period material. The team is preparing a guide to pixel art, resolution and gameplay, she said.

The movie, directed by Siân Heder and starring Daisy Edgar-Jones, adapts Gabrielle Zevin’s best-selling novel about game developers.

Van Beek pointed to the success of “The Last of Us” and “Fallout” as evidence of the growing flow of video game intellectual property into film and television. “The other way around, it almost doesn’t really happen anymore,” he said, recalling the proliferation of movie-based games in the 1990s. However, he cautioned that adaptations remain challenging because much of the original interactive experience can be lost.

The convergence also extends to how studios assess audience reactions. In detail, Velazquez revealed that “God of War” development incorporates scheduled play-tests, facial recordings, eye tracking and detailed surveys examining narrative comprehension and difficulty. “We actually have eye tracking software where we actually see where their eyes are going,” he explained. “Are they looking at where we want them to look at certain moments?” Such feedback has become integral to the production process.

For Hickel, technological sophistication does not necessarily guarantee a better character performance. Discussing “The Mandalorian and Grogu,” he explained how ILM determines when to retain Grogu as a physical puppet and when digital intervention is necessary. “Sometimes the puppetiness is exactly the effect you want on the audience’s brain,” he said, noting that viewers appreciate the character’s “muppety quality,” even if certain movements require digital corrections.

Hickel also described how the production used virtual reality to scout digital environments and simulate different seating positions inside an IMAX auditorium. Apple Vision Pro proved particularly useful for judging the scale of sets before physical construction. “We could really understand the space and know how big it was, and which parts were going to be built practically,” he recalled.

The conversation also addressed AI, with Velazquez comparing current anxieties to earlier fears that computer animation and motion capture would eliminate traditional animation jobs. Both technologies ultimately expanded artists’ capabilities, he argued. “You still need that creative mind. You still need a team of creatives to come together and use these tools,” he said. “But if you don’t have the soul behind it, it’s not going to matter.”

Van Beek took a more cautious position, warning about the potential misuse of AI and the appropriation of other artists’ work. “People are going to use it for really great things and really terrible things,” he underscored. Hickel, meanwhile, distinguished the uncertainty facing professional employment from the enduring ability to create art. “There’s no technical innovation that’s going to stop people from making art and finding ways to make art,” he argued, suggesting that new types of animation and VFX companies may eventually emerge.

Despite increasingly sophisticated tools, the panelists stressed that technology alone will not secure a career. Velazquez said he would rather recruit someone who collaborates effectively than a technically stronger candidate with a poor attitude, while DeMarco emphasized the importance of communication, constructive feedback and adaptability when moving between disciplines.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Kay Cannon has found her next studio directing vehicle: Single at the Wedding , a romantic comedy that she’ll re-write and direct for New Line Cinema.

The title tells you what to expect here: the film follows Allie, who as the last single one of her friends, is determined to find love at her best friend’s wedding.

Cannon will team with Eben Russell, creator of the Freeform comedy series Alone Together , for a new pass on the original screenplay by Anne Sundell, which was originally developed by Sundell and Alex Richanbach.

Related Stories

New Line Boss Richard Brener Poised To Jump To Merged Paramount-Warner Bros - The Dish

'Army Of Thieves' Matthias Schweighöfer Latest To Join New Line's 'The Conjuring: First Communion'

Joe Roth and Jeff Kirschenbaum, veterans of such recent rom-coms as the Sony hit Anyone But You and Netflix’s A Family Affair , are producing. Cannon will exec produce alongside Richanbach.

Watch on Deadline

No stranger to the rom-com herself, Cannon is coming off One Attempt Remaining , starring Jennifer Garner and John Cena — another film that she co-wrote and directed. That title, from 21 Laps and Linden Entertainment, has not yet locked in a release date.

An Emmy nominee, Cannon is otherwise known for creating the a capella comedy franchise Pitch Perfect and for her feature directorial debut, the hit Uni comedy Blockers , also starring Cena. Following her work there, she went on to write and direct a jukebox musical take on Cinderella , starring singer-songwriter Camila Cabello, for Columbia Pictures/Amazon. On the television side, her credits include six seasons of 30 Rock , for which she earned multiple Emmy nominations, Writers Guild Awards and a Peabody Award, along with Fox’s New Girl , where she was Co-EP, and Netflix’s Girlboss , which she created.

New Line has a long history of producing comedic crowd-pleasers, from the Friday , Austin Powers and Rush Hour film franchises to such hit one-offs as Wedding Crashers , The Wedding Singer , and Elf .

Single at the Wedding will mark Cannon’s first outing with the studio, which yesterday announced One of Them Days ‘ Lawrence Lamont as directing the next installment in their Friday franchise with Ice Cube. She is repped by by WME and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller.

editorial_title_zh: The Lens of Time：当眼镜成为电影的主角
editorial_excerpt_zh: 一场展览通过设计、手工艺和大银幕讲述意大利眼镜制造业的历史。费里尼和马斯托依安尼的眼镜也在展出之列，展览路线与罗马电影节交相辉映。文章 The Lens of Time：当眼镜…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "正当罗马电影节在音乐公园礼堂（Auditorium Parco della Musica）拉开帷幕之际，在距离活动核心区仅几步之遥的皮亚琴蒂尼宫（Palazzo Piacentini，即意大利企业暨“意大利制造”部所在地）大厅内，电影史与当代美学中最具辨识度的配饰之一的历史交织在了一起。由意大利国家光学制品制造商协会（ANFAO）联合皮韦迪卡多雷眼镜博物馆（Museo dell’Occhiale di Pieve di Cadore）发起、并获得意大利企业暨“意大利制造”部（MIMIT）赞助的名为“The Lens of Time”的展览向公众开放，展期至2026年30月。展览呈现了一段跨越数百年历史的旅程，从最初眼镜的诞生到当代的技术实验，聚焦于制造工艺、身份认同与视觉表征之间的关系。这一展览路线将电影视作其最重要的篇章之一，展示了一个为矫正视力而诞生的物件如何转变为心理刻画、角色塑造和风格定义的工具。", "links": [{"text": "Festa del Cinema di Roma", "url": "https://www.mimit.gov.it/it/?view=article&id=2048158&catid=8"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Occhiali-Carlo-Verdone-1024x576.jpeg", "alt": "lens of time ", "caption": "带有“后视镜”的太阳镜，与卡洛·韦尔多内（Carlo Verdone）在电影《蜜月旅行》中佩戴的款式相同，Goggs型号，博士伦（Bausch & Lomb），90年代，卢奇奥·斯特拉马雷（Lucio Stramare）收藏", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "眼镜的起源可追溯至13世纪末。关于其生产的最早记录来自威尼斯，见于1300年4月2日的玻璃工会章程（Capitolari dei Cristalleri）中。自那时起，镜框历经各个时代与变革，顺应着工艺与审美的演变。19世纪，无镜腿、依靠弹簧系统固定在鼻梁上的夹鼻眼镜（pince-nez）广为流行；而1878年则标志着意大利眼镜工业的一个转折点，卡拉尔佐迪卡多雷（Calalzo di Cadore）诞生了第一家眼镜工厂。正是基于这一传统，孕育出一段推动“意大利制造”走向国际声誉的制造历史。但在大银幕上，眼镜获得了更深维度的意义。它不再仅仅是一件配饰，而是一个能够诉说佩戴者身份、暗示神秘感、权威感、讽刺感或距离感的元素。在1953年的电影《如何嫁给一个百万富翁》中，玛丽莲·梦露（Marilyn Monroe）助力确立了猫眼框（cat-eye）的地位，将其转化为魅力与诱惑的象征。在此后的岁月里，宽大的太阳镜成为银幕女神形象不可或缺的一部分，正如碧姬·巴铎（Brigitte Bardot）所选择的由卢奇奥·斯特拉马雷收藏的洛扎（Lozza）Zilo型号所证明的那样。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Occhiali-Federico-Fellini-1024x576.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "费代里科·费里尼（Federico Fellini）的眼镜，Persol Ratti，20世纪70年代，意大利都灵，亚历山德罗·斯皮齐亚（Alessandro Spiezia）收藏", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览还为电影主角们佩戴的眼镜留出了空间。2013年电影《黑金杀机》中布拉德·皮特（Brad Pitt）所佩戴的 Cazal Targa Design 眼镜（此处展出的是一款80年代末的白色版本），突显了韦斯特雷（Westray）这一角色自信且炫耀的形象。1998年电影《恐惧拉斯维加斯》中约翰尼·德普（Johnny Depp）佩戴的黄色镜片雷朋（Ray-Ban）射手（Shooter）眼镜，则直接让人联想到作家亨特·S·汤普森（Hunter S. Thompson），该电影正是改编自他的同名书籍。除了这些物品之外，费代里科·费里尼和马尔切洛·马斯托依安尼（Marcello Mastroianni）的眼镜唤起了配饰与电影身份之间深厚的联系。费里尼佩戴着宽大的光学镜框，让-吕克·戈达尔（Jean-Luc Godard）几乎总是藏在墨镜后面，莉娜·韦特缪勒（Lina Wertmüller）将白色眼镜变成了一种视觉签名，皮埃尔·保罗·帕索里尼（Pier Paolo Pasolini）则是镜框如何成为作者公众形象密不可分的一部分的例证。 Akira Kurosawa（黑泽明）也经常求助于墨镜，将其转化为自己与世界之间一道象征性的屏障。与电影的对话同样通过那些让电影历史成为现实的工具展开。两台电影摄影机记录了拍摄技术的演变：一台是1927年的蔡司伊康 Kinamo（Zeiss Ikon Kinamo），小巧且适合手持拍摄；另一台是于1958年推出的博略 R16（Beaulieu R16），因其在纪录片和独立制作中的多功能性而备受赞赏。这些物件讲述了视觉的另一场革命，那场改变了观察与呈现现实方式的革命。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Occhiali-Lily-Collins-1024x576.jpeg", "alt": "lens of time ", "caption": "与电视剧《艾米丽在巴黎》主角莉莉·柯林斯（Lily Collins）在2021年佩戴的同款太阳镜，意大利，L.G.R.，TWIGA型号", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从70年代夸张的大号镜框、大胆的色彩和戏剧性的装饰，到智能眼镜以及高级制造工艺的新实验，“The Lens of Time”展示了对眼镜的研究如何在功能、设计和创新之间不断前行。借着电影节的契机，展览邀请人们超越表面去观察，认识到眼镜是一台虽小却具决定性的叙事机器，它能够穿梭于视觉文化的历史之中，并在集体记忆中留下印记。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Mentre all’Auditorium Parco della Musica si accendono i riflettori sulla Festa del Cinema di Roma , a pochi passi dal cuore della manifestazione, nelle sale di Palazzo Piacentini, sede del Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy, la storia del cinema si intreccia con quella di uno degli accessori più riconoscibili dell’immaginario contemporaneo. Si intitola The Lens of Time la mostra promossa da ANFAO, l’Associazione Nazionale Fabbricanti Articoli Ottici, in collaborazione con il Museo dell’Occhiale di Pieve di Cadore e con il patrocinio del MIMIT, aperta al pubblico fino al 30 ottobre 2026. L’esposizione propone un viaggio attraverso secoli di storia, dalla nascita dei primi occhiali alla sperimentazione tecnologica contemporanea, mettendo al centro il rapporto tra manifattura, identità e rappresentazione. Un percorso che trova proprio nel cinema uno dei suoi capitoli più significativi, mostrando come un oggetto nato per correggere la vista possa trasformarsi in uno strumento di caratterizzazione psicologica, costruzione del personaggio e definizione dello stile.

Le origini degli occhiali risalgono alla fine del XIII secolo. La più antica testimonianza della loro produzione è veneziana e compare nei Capitolari dei Cristalleri del 2 aprile 1300. Da allora, le montature hanno attraversato epoche e trasformazioni, seguendo l’evoluzione delle tecniche e del gusto. Nell’Ottocento si diffondono i pince-nez, senza aste e fissati al naso grazie a un sistema a molla, mentre il 1878 segna una svolta per l’industria italiana con la nascita della prima fabbrica di occhiali a Calalzo di Cadore. Da questa tradizione prende forma una storia produttiva che contribuirà all’affermazione internazionale del Made in Italy. Ma è sul grande schermo che l’occhiale acquista una dimensione ulteriore. Non è più soltanto un accessorio, ma un elemento capace di raccontare chi lo indossa, suggerendo mistero, autorevolezza, ironia o distanza. In Come sposare un milionario del 1953, Marilyn Monroe contribuisce a consacrare la montatura cat-eye, trasformandola in un simbolo di glamour e seduzione. Negli anni successivi, le grandi montature da sole diventano parte integrante dell’immagine delle dive, come testimonia il modello Zilo di Lozza scelto da Brigitte Bardot, proveniente dalla collezione Lucio Stramare.

La mostra dedica spazio anche agli occhiali indossati dai protagonisti del cinema. I Cazal Targa Design associati a Brad Pitt nel film The Counselor del 2013, qui rappresentati da una versione bianca della fine degli anni Ottanta, accentuano l’immagine sicura e ostentata del personaggio Westray. I Ray-Ban Shooter dalle lenti gialle indossati da Johnny Depp in Paura e delirio a Las Vegas del 1998 rimandano invece direttamente allo scrittore Hunter S. Thompson, autore del libro da cui il film è tratto. Accanto a questi oggetti, gli occhiali di Federico Fellini e Marcello Mastroianni evocano un legame profondo tra accessorio e identità cinematografica. Fellini, con le sue ampie montature da vista, Jean-Luc Godard, quasi sempre dietro lenti scure, Lina Wertmüller, che fa degli occhiali bianchi una firma visiva, e Pier Paolo Pasolini sono esempi di come una montatura possa diventare parte inseparabile dell’immagine pubblica di un autore. Anche Akira Kurosawa ricorre spesso agli occhiali scuri, trasformandoli in una barriera simbolica tra sé e il mondo. Il dialogo con il cinema passa anche attraverso gli strumenti che ne hanno reso possibile la storia. Due cineprese documentano l’evoluzione della ripresa, dalla Zeiss Ikon Kinamo del 1927, compatta e adatta alle riprese a mano libera, alla Beaulieu R16, presentata nel 1958 e apprezzata per la sua versatilità nel documentario e nelle produzioni indipendenti. Oggetti che raccontano un’altra rivoluzione dello sguardo, quella che ha cambiato il modo di osservare e rappresentare la realtà.

Dagli anni Settanta, con le montature oversize, i colori audaci e le decorazioni teatrali, fino agli smart glasses e alle nuove sperimentazioni di alta manifattura, The Lens of Time mostra come la ricerca sull’occhiale continui a muoversi tra funzione, design e innovazione. In occasione della Festa del Cinema, la mostra invita così a guardare oltre la superficie, riconoscendo negli occhiali una piccola ma decisiva macchina narrativa, capace di attraversare la storia della cultura visiva e di lasciare un segno nella memoria collettiva.

article_text:
Mostri, divinità, giocattoli e figure umane dalle sembianze animali popolano le opere di Alberto Savinio , artista e intellettuale che ha attraversato la cultura europea del Novecento senza lasciarsi ricondurre a un solo linguaggio. Fratello minore di Giorgio de Chirico , con cui condivide alcune delle premesse della pittura metafisica, Savinio ha sviluppato una ricerca autonoma, alimentata dalla letteratura, dalla musica e da una continua rielaborazione delle immagini del passato. Dal 30 ottobre 2026 al 4 aprile 2027, la Pinacoteca Agnelli di Torino gli dedica Alberto Savinio. Souvenir , una retrospettiva a cura di Sarah Cosulich e Pietro Rigolo , assistiti da Raphaële Sevrain , che riunisce più di settanta opere e ripercorre i principali temi della sua produzione, dalla mitologia all’infanzia, dal grottesco alla metamorfosi. Le opere provengono dai principali musei italiani, ma anche da istituzioni parigine e viennesi, unitamente a prestiti da collezioni private. Il titolo, invece, richiama il ruolo fondamentale che la memoria assume nell’opera dell’artista, intesa come un repertorio di immagini da selezionare e ricombinare, un processo creativo attraverso il quale esperienze personali, miti collettivi e frammenti della cultura occidentale vengono trasformati in nuove configurazioni simboliche. Fotografie familiari, illustrazioni, atlanti geografici e riferimenti alla statuaria classica convivono nei suoi dipinti secondo una logica di accostamenti inattesi, che vedono ricordi personali e immaginario collettivo sovrapporsi e mescolarsi.

Il percorso espositivo si articola attorno a nuclei tematici che restituiscono la varietà di questa ricerca, dai cosiddetti «giocattoli» alle figure ibride, fino ai disegni e alle opere in cui il mito diventa uno strumento per interrogare il presente. La mostra invita a rileggere Savinio alla luce di questioni ancora attuali, come il rapporto tra umano e non umano, la trasformazione delle immagini e il confine tra realtà e immaginazione, sottolineando come la modernità di questo artista risieda proprio nella capacità di guardare al passato non come a un repertorio fisso e immobile, ma come a una risorsa per pensare a ciò che ancora non esiste e non si può scorgere, ma si può immaginare.

Ecco cinque cose da sapere prima di visitare la retrospettiva.

Alberto Savinio: la multidisciplinarietà e l’amicizia con altri artisti

Musicista di formazione, scrittore, drammaturgo, giornalista, saggista e scenografo, oltre che pittore, Alberto Savinio – pseudonimo di Andrea Francesco Alberto de Chirico – nasce ad Atene il 25 agosto 1891. La sua formazione musicale precede l’attività pittorica: studia composizione e pianoforte al Conservatorio di Atene, diplomandosi nel 1903 all’età di dodici anni e proseguendo gli studi musicali a Monaco di Baviera nel 1906, dove la sua famiglia si era trasferita temporaneamente in seguito alla morte del padre. Durante il suo primo viaggio a Parigi, nel 1910, entra in contatto con gli ambienti delle avanguardie e con figure come quella di Guillaume Apollinaire , che ne sostiene e incoraggia il lavoro e lo mette in contatto con figure della cerchia artica di Apollinaire, come Pablo Picasso , Max Jacob e Francis Picabia . Nel 1914 presenta Les Chants de la Mi-Mort , un poema drammatico accompagnato da una composizione musicale per pianoforte e adotta per la prima volta lo pseudonimo che lo accompagnerà poi per tutta la sua carriera. La scrittura e la musica rimarranno componenti essenziali della sua attività, anche quando la pittura assumerà un ruolo sempre più importante.

Questa pluralità, questa compresenza dà voce a un universo simbolico e a un patrimonio mitico comune, nel quale parole, immagini e suoni possono essere rielaborati e messi in relazione. La sua attività di scrittore comprende opere come Hermaphrodito (1918), mentre i suoi interventi critici testimoniano un interesse costante per la cultura antica, la filosofia e le contraddizioni della modernità.

Nel 1915, a seguito dello scoppio della Prima Guerra Mondiale e dei suoi primi, devastanti risvolti, Savinio e il fratello tornano in Italia e vengono arruolati e mandati a Ferrara, dove incontrarono Filippo de Pisis e Carlo Carrà , figure chiave per la costruzione dell’immaginario metafisico per la cui costituzione Savinio avrebbe svolto un ruolo cruciale.

La pittura di Savinio va quindi letta anche alla luce di questa formazione multidisciplinare, con le sue opere che sembrano tradurre in forme visive un pensiero che si estrinseca attraverso citazioni e accostamenti inattesi.

La Metafisica lo riguarda, ma non lo esaurisce

Il rapporto con Giorgio de Chirico influenzò la produzione pittorica, anche perché i due fratelli condividevano l’interesse per il mito, per la sospensione temporale e per l’alone di enigma che aleggi attorno gli oggetti e delle figure protagonisti nelle opere dei due. Savinio, tuttavia, elabora una poetica personale, nella quale l’ironia e la trasformazione delle forme assumono un ruolo centrale e il suo contributo alla cultura metafisica precede la piena affermazione della sua pittura. Nel 1914, con Les Chants de la Mi-Mort , introduce la figura di un uomo senza voce, senza occhi e senza volto in un contesto teatrale e musicale, negli stessi anni in cui lo stesso motivo apparirà nella nella pittura del fratello e nella sua stessa produzione successiva, assumendo un ruolo di grande rilievo. I manichini di Savinio diventano quindi esseri ambigui, a metà tra umano e artificiale, capaci di mettere in discussione l’identità e la forma del corpo.

Negli anni Venti, quando si dedica più intensamente alla pittura, sviluppa composizioni nelle quali figure provenienti da epoche diverse convivono in spazi sospesi, simili a scenografie. In Le tendre quatuor (Hommage à Raphaël) del 1928, per esempio, i personaggi assumono sembianze meccaniche e prive di volto. La modernità, per Savinio, non coincide con il rifiuto della tradizione, ma al contrario può nascere proprio dal suo riutilizzo e dalla sua riscrittura.

I suoi quadri sono anche archivi di memoria

Il titolo della mostra, Souvenir , richiama uno dei principi fondamentali della ricerca di Savinio, intendendo la memoria come catalogo di immagini da trasformare: ricordi personali, fotografie di famiglia, illustrazioni, atlanti geografici e esempi di statuaria classica possono entrare nella stessa composizione, perdendo la loro funzione originaria per assumere nuovi significati.

Un esempio è Senza titolo – Couple et enfant del 1927, nel quale l’artista accosta una rappresentazione di Ercole bambino – tratta da un repertorio di scultura greco-romana – a fotografie dei propri genitori, Evaristo e Gemma. Il risultato è una sorta di collage dipinto, in cui fonti differenti vengono ricomposte senza cancellare del tutto la loro provenienza. Le figure sembrano appartenere a tempi diversi, ma la loro convivenza nello stesso spazio rende possibile una nuova narrazione. Il passato viene quindi sottoposto a un processo di selezione e trasformazione che rende visibili connessioni altrimenti difficili da cogliere, e il mito assume la medesima funzione, con divinità ed eroi dell’antichità non più confinati in un mondo lontano, ma partecipi appieno della quotidianità, talvolta travestiti da personaggi borghesi o da animali.

Mostri, animali e mobili mettono in crisi i confini tra le cose

A partire dagli anni Trenta, la pittura di Savinio si popola sempre più frequentemente di figure ibride: uomini con teste di uccello, creature dalla fisionomia preistorica, corpi che si fondono con oggetti d’arredo e personaggi dalle sembianze mostruose introducono un principio di metamorfosi che attraversa tutta la sua opera.

In Autoritratto in forma di gufo del 1936, l’artista si rappresenta attraverso un animale associato alla saggezza e alla dea Atena, richiamando anche la propria nascita ad Atene. In Una strana famiglia del 1947, invece, i volti di padre, madre e figlia sono nascosti da escrescenze colorate che impediscono di riconoscerne le espressioni. L’immagine del nucleo familiare, tradizionalmente associata a un ideale di armonia domestica, viene così trasformata in una scena grottesca e ambigua.

Anche i mobili possono assumere una dimensione antropomorfa; le poltrone, in particolare, sembrano custodire le tracce di chi le ha utilizzate, fino a fondersi con i corpi e a diventare parte di una mitologia personale.

I giocattoli come monumenti dedicati all’infanzia

Tra il 1928 e il 1930 Savinio realizza una serie di dipinti dedicati ai giocattoli, tra i nuclei più riconoscibili della sua produzione. Forme geometriche dai colori vivaci si accumulano in composizioni che evocano paesaggi, isole, coste e scenari di esplorazione. In opere come L’isola dei giocattoli del 1930, gli oggetti sembrano costruire un mondo autonomo, sospeso tra il gioco e la rappresentazione monumentale. L’infanzia rappresenta per Savinio un momento in cui l’immaginazione può ancora organizzare il mondo secondo possibilità molteplici, prima che l’educazione e la razionalità ne restringano le interpretazioni e i giocattoli diventano in quest’ottica immagini ambivalenti, che evocano la libertà creativa, ma anche la nostalgia per una condizione destinata a finire.

Il motivo dell’isola rafforza questa dimensione: luogo separato dal mondo e insieme possibile approdo, spazio alternativo, nel quale le regole della realtà possono essere sospese. In L’isola approdata del 1950, ad esempio, l’immagine si lega a una riflessione più ampia sulla metamorfosi che vede non solo l’uomo trasformarsi, ma anche un paesaggio che può acquisire una propria vitalità.

Il disegno è un linguaggio autonomo, non un semplice esercizio preparatorio

Nella produzione dell’artista, il disegno costituisce un campo di sperimentazione indipendente, nel quale l’artista mette alla prova tecniche e soluzioni visive differenti, dal collage al pastello, dall’inchiostro al carboncino. I primi esperimenti, degli anni 1925-1926, presentano ritagli di giornale, inserti tessili e riferimenti alla statuaria classica e al viaggio. A partire dalla metà degli anni Trenta, il disegno acquista ulteriore importanza, anche in relazione all’intensificarsi dell’attività letteraria. Alcune opere accompagnano testi propri o di altri autori, mentre altre sviluppano immagini indipendenti dalla scrittura.

Il mito è una chiave per interpretare il presente

Divinità, eroi e creature della mitologia greca attraversano la pittura di Savinio, ma non vengono rappresentati come figure appartenenti a un passato concluso, quanto piuttosto come un repertorio attraverso cui interrogare l’esperienza contemporanea e la propria biografia. Le storie antiche entrano in contatto con fotografie familiari, ambienti borghesi e oggetti quotidiani, generando situazioni nelle quali epoche e riferimenti differenti convivono.

In Bataille de Centaures (1930), per esempio, il riferimento alla centauromachia – la battaglia mitologica tra Centauri e Lapiti – si intreccia con una riflessione sul conflitto tra ordine e caos. Le creature dipinte dall’artista, con i loro colli allungati e le forme che richiamano animali preistorici, si allontanano dalla rappresentazione tradizionale dei centauri e assumono un aspetto inquietante, a metà tra il mostruoso e il primordiale.

Anche in opere come La Visitation (1930), i riferimenti biblici si sovrappongono a suggestioni classiche e autobiografiche, rendendo incerta una lettura univoca dell’immagine.

title_original: Tony Gilroy on the Lunch With Pedro Pascal That Saved ‘Behemoth!’ and How the Film Explores ‘New Varieties of Loneliness’
editorial_title_zh: 托尼·吉尔罗伊谈与佩德罗·帕斯卡那场拯救了《Behemoth!》的午餐，以及该片如何探讨“新型孤独”
editorial_excerpt_zh: 托尼·吉尔罗伊在去见佩德罗·帕斯卡的路上已经准备好了说辞。他在去吃午餐的车里反复排练。奥斯卡·伊萨克退出了《Behemoth!》，由于吉尔罗伊所说的“《弗兰肯斯坦》与颁奖季之间的交通堵塞”而无缘该片，这位编剧兼导演已经将他的这部新片开机日期推迟到了极限——片中讲述了一名大提琴手在离开20年后重返洛杉矶的故事。于是，他和制片人萨妮·沃尔伦伯格开车去见帕斯卡，但吉尔罗伊已经想好了要对集结好的剧组说些什么：“我们真的尽力了。我们现在不拍这部电影了。我会为大伙找点别的活。”

"paragraph", "text": "这个创意是在《侠盗一号：星球大战外传》的配乐录制现场产生的，当时他观看了迈克尔·贾基诺的作曲录制。随后，吉尔罗伊花了六个月时间采访各行各业的音乐家，然后《安多》便彻底将他吞噬。当他重新露面时，他说，他“非常渴望一个避难所”，以逃离那部剧集的愤怒与政治纷争。他在一部关于电影音乐的电影中找到了这个避难所，而他随即把这部电影的融资难度做到了极致。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这是一部关于大提琴手的电影。祝你好运，”他在阐述电影构思时说道，“故事发生在破碎的时空中。我大概需要9位作曲家。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部电影无法在亚特兰大或澳大利亚拍摄。现场需要303位工会音乐家。“这部电影的边缘成本可能和《夜行者》[的总成本]相当。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这9位作曲家——迈克尔·阿贝尔斯（《逃出绝命镇》）、钢琴家兼作曲家艾米莉·贝尔、卢卡斯·弗兰克、迈克尔·贾基诺（《飞屋环游记》）、詹姆斯·纽顿·霍华德（《迈克尔·克莱顿》）、亨利·杰克曼（《美国队长2：冬日战士》）、纳米·梅卢马德（皮克斯的《梦境制片厂》）、布兰登·罗伯茨（《安多》）和亚伦·西尔维斯特里（《阿甘正传》）——在演职员表中仅署名为“Behemoth!集体”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这9人的合作条款完全一致：相同的酬金、按字母顺序排列的演职员表、平等的署名、海报上不出现个人名字、所有人都享有版权分成。“非常、非常、非常少的钱，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当经纪人们开始打电话询问他在做什么时，他已经签下了两位半作曲家。等他完成时，作曲家们已经开始主动给他打电话了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吉尔罗伊不希望《Behemoth!》被拿来与托德·菲尔德执导、凯特·布兰切特主演的《塔尔》进行比较，他也不希望人们把它描述成一部古典音乐电影，他认为这会让电影“听起来像菠菜一样难以下咽”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他更希望观众将之听作一部关于家庭的电影，以及关于他在碎片化世界中所说的“新型孤独”的电影。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他说，最令他心碎的是“太迟了”这句话。他已经结婚43年了，有一个孙辈，并且和兄弟们以及团队关系极其紧密。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "url": "https://variety.com/lists/2027-oscars-predictions/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我不知道这是习惯成自然还是出于对祖传领地的记忆，多年来我完全把自己塑造成了契合128页剧本和两小时体验的模式。六个月的筹备，六个月的拍摄，这种为期18个月的农耕式系统。这是一个伟大的系统。我无法想象去做一件很长的事情，然后我真的渴望去做它了。但担任剧集统筹就像是超级导演。其实没太大区别。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我最终在《侠盗一号》与迈克尔·贾基诺合作配乐期间萌生了这个想法。能在现场实在太令人兴奋了。那里一定有一部电影。在那之后，我花了六个月时间采访音乐家。一个人会把我引向另一个人。其中有来自《侠盗一号》和《迈克尔·克莱顿》的音乐家，也有我多年来结识的人。电影新闻非常有意思，因为人们会对你撒谎、编造内容，但你确实能从中获得本质的真相。大家会告诉你很多事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我知道得很多，但我没有找到抓手。接着我被卷入了《安多》。在《安多》经历了漫长的后期制作之后，你有时间去琢磨下一步想做什么。我想远离《安多》的愤怒、政治和喧嚣。我渴望得到一个避难所，哪怕只是片刻，好清醒一下头脑。所以我格外努力地去寻找那个抓手，而我找到了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "每个人站起来都会说：“哦，这太棒了、太精彩了。”我只是顺应这个好莱坞式的恭维列车，因为我讲不出别的事。这这家伙从第一天起就无可挑剔。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当奥斯卡退出时，《弗兰肯斯坦》与颁奖季之间撞期了，我又试着推进了一次。我不想失去我的团队，但我也不想再勉强推进下去了。突然之间，佩德罗出现了。珊妮和我出去和他在午餐时碰面，我在车里正排练着要对团队说的那番话：“嘿，我们真的很努力了，但我们现在不拍这部电影了。我要试着为我们找点别的活儿。”留住团队很难。所以我们在去吃午餐时，我一直在准备那段令人失望的致辞。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "过了10分钟，我就想：“哦天哪，他怎么能这么完美？他一定是的。他身上肯定有什么不对劲。有什么问题吗？”他是个才华横溢的演员、完全的天然派，又能唱又能跳。但他在每一个镜头、每一个时刻都在场，而且他没多少台词。我希望这部电影能带点火花。我想为那个叹号作个辩护。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们开了一个三小时的会，与其说是开会，不如说更像是一份婚前协议，因为大概半小时后我们就决定了：“行，我们喜欢你，你也喜欢我们，谁也没在兜售什么。”会议就该是这样的。我们说：“这就是我们需要的一切”，他说：“这就是我需要的。”接着他说：“我明天就开始。”第二天，他手里就拿上大提琴了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "40多天。我们的前期筹备有五、六个月。这是一部极度依赖前期的电影，筹备量巨大。要在资金有限的情况下拍出这么大体量的电影，你必须做足前期筹备。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这是一部关于大提琴手的电影。祝你好运。故事发生在碎片化的时间里。我可能需要9位作曲家。哦，对了，我们绝不可能去亚特兰大或澳大利亚拍摄。我们在拍一部关于珊瑚礁消失的电影。那会违背这部电影的核心立意。我们需要雇用303名工会音乐家，我们必须在洛杉矶拍摄。我们必须支付所有的附加福利。这部电影的附加福利成本可能和《夜行者》的总成本差不多。所以这确实是个难题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个推介很有趣。“嘿，我在拍一部关于你们这个世界的电影。你想读读剧本吗？我在搞这么个极其荒唐的玩意儿。”对前几个人，我的态度是：“如果你不喜欢或者不感兴趣，那就当没这回事。如果你喜欢，我们晚点再跟经纪人们对接，因为这里没钱。不过请先读一读再打电话。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我知道我能请到詹姆斯·纽顿·霍华德，因为这些年来我和他关系最密切。我觉得他会来做最后收尾的部分，所以我心里有一个定海神针。詹姆斯会把结尾的《Behemoth》部分彻底做绝。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "亨利·杰克曼是第一个加入的。我们的音乐总监——在很多这方面的工作中她是那个无名英雄——说：“我觉得亨利会对这个非常感兴趣。”我们很快碰了面，他立刻就加入了。然后他开始帮我牵线搭桥。在经纪人开始打电话质问“他妈的你在搞什么鬼？为什么在给我的客户打电话”之前，我已经签下了两个半作曲家。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "合作条款始终如一。我绝不会让任何人去演反差角色。那有什么意义呢？无论你是谁，每个人的酬劳都一样。有些人要干的活比别人多得多，但大家都拿一样的钱。演职员署名永远挂在Behemoth Collective（贝希摩斯合集）名下，永远按字母顺序排列，永远享有平等的署名权。在海报上，我们只写这个集体。我们绝不放个人名字。我们为所有人争取到了版权收益，虽然我不太确定这是否创下了先例，但它似乎非常罕见。钱非常、非常、非常少。每个人对混音都有最终决定权。这就是基本规则。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "等我敲定后，还有几个人想加入，但我已经没有位置了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "探照灯影业要做一个幕后花絮短片，原声带也会上线Spotify。他们会在宣传上全面发力。但我不知道这在电影里具体该怎么呈现。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这完全写在纸面上。我不知道《综艺》杂志对电影之神作何感想，但这是我笃信的宗教，在选角方面，电影之神确实对我很眷顾。我拿下了佩德罗。然后我有几个凭直觉最先想找的女演员，但要么没档期，要么合作不成。接着奥利维亚的名字被提了出来，我就想：哦天哪，我们为什么不一开始就找她呢？她会怎么说？我想我在12小时内就收到了她的回复。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我指导过很多导演。指导导演有种特别纯粹的爽感，尤其是像她这么聪明的人。我说：“你想问什么问题我都回答你。卡萝尔在任何争论中都不会输。她只会宣告胜利然后走开。其他任何事我都可以告诉你。”她说：“不用，我懂了。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她的戏份就是为什么你不需要排练的头号证据。如果情况复杂或者有新东西，我会排练；但总的来说，当那些硬核内容在银幕上流淌时，我不仅想看佩德罗，还想看剧组每个人的反应。不需要拍很多条。她走过来，往那儿一站，台词脱口而出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果你说这是关于音乐和大提琴的——我讨厌用古典音乐这个词，因为里面大多是电影配乐——听起来就会像在吃菠菜。听起来会死板沉闷，好像这部电影纯粹是为了你好一样。但实际上，这是关于家庭和家族历史的，是关于世界上如何涌现出如此之多的新型孤独。过去，孤独往往只局限于少数几种范畴。而现在，孤独的方式有千万种，随着社会日趋碎片化，人们也愈发孤独。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我也觉得“中年危机”这个词挺好，能让人们脑子里有个概念：人活一辈子确实会经历危机，但时间点并不准。我们会有各种各样的至暗或转折时刻，它们在不同的时间节点降临。会有一种决定性的时刻，觉得哪里不对劲，某种突如其来的探索，某种未完成的事情必须去处理、不去管或者逃避。我们每个人都有。所以从家庭动力学和家庭戏剧的角度来看，我认为这是一部极具普世价值的家庭电影，有着非常动人、希望能带来宣泄的结局。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部电影里的角色和你正在一起解开同一个谜题。我们为什么要走到这一步？为什么要追溯到20年前？他在结尾时提出了一个大得无以复加的问题，而你成了他解题的同行者。这是一部很不寻常的电影。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我其实不太喜欢我们被拿来和《Tár》作比较。我之所以不太喜欢这个对比，是因为我觉得佩德罗的角色并不是一个纵欲者。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当你演奏音乐时，你会拥有一个能自动把你带入社群的出口，而纽约本身就像是一个大家庭。但天哪，当你收拾好琴盒回家时，你就只剩下你自己了。对亚历克斯来说，童年时期施加在他身上的要求、为了维持状态而不得不做出的角色转换，以及他那四海为家的游牧生活，让他很容易去习惯于满足所有人的期盼。你虽然永远无法真正给予人们真正需要的东西，但你确实能满足所有人的期盼。这种组合在外人看来或许非常有趣、非常时髦，但天哪。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
Tony Gilroy had the speech ready on his way to meet Pedro Pascal . He was rehearsing it in the car on the way to lunch.

Oscar Isaac was out of “ Behemoth !,” lost to what Gilroy calls “a traffic jam between ‘Frankenstein’ and awards,” and the writer-director had already pushed the start date as far as he was willing to push it for his new film about a cello player who returns to Los Angeles after 20 years. So he and producer Sanne Wohlenberg drove to meet Pascal, but Gilroy had already worked out what he would say to the crew he had assembled: “We tried really hard. We’re not doing this movie now. I’ll find us something else.”

“10 minutes into lunch, I’m like, ‘Oh my God, can he be this perfect?’” Gilroy tells Variety over coffee on the final morning of the Middleburg Film Festival. “There must be something wrong with him.”

There wasn’t. A three-hour meeting followed that Gilroy describes as “more of a prenup than a meeting.” By the next day, Pascal was learning the cello.

The result is Gilroy’s first feature as a director since 2012′ “The Bourne Legacy” and his first anything since Disney+’s “Andor,” the two-season series that consumed most of his last six years. Pascal plays Alex Serian, a cellist from a family of studio musicians who comes home to Los Angeles after two decades on the road and starts recording film scores, including a giant studio production with the secret title “Behemoth!” The film is among the Oscar contenders this year including best actor for Pascal, and with the strong reviews, perhaps even best picture. The cast also includes Olivia Wilde, Will Arnett, Eva Victor, Alexa Swinton and Hank Azaria.

The idea arrived on the scoring stage for “Rogue One: A Star Wars Story,” after watching Michael Giacchino’s composing sessions. Gilroy then spent six months interviewing working musicians before “Andor” swallowed him whole. When he surfaced, he says, he was “very eager for a sanctuary” from the anger and politics of that show. He found it in a movie about movie music, which he immediately made as difficult as possible to finance.

“It’s a movie about a cellist. Good luck,” he says, running down the movie pitch. “Takes place in fractured time. I’m probably going to need nine composers.”

It could not be shot in Atlanta or Australia. It needed 303 union musicians on the stage. “The fringes on this movie probably cost what ‘Nightcrawler’ cost [in total].”

Those nine composers — Michael Abels (“Get Out”) along with pianist and composer Emily Bear, Lukas Frank, Michael Giacchino (“Up”), James Newton Howard (“Michael Clayton”), Henry Jackman (“Captain America: The Winter Soldier”), Nami Melumad (Pixar’s “Dream Productions”), Brandon Roberts (“Andor”) and Alan Silvestri (“Forrest Gump”) — are billed only as “The Behemoth! Collective.”

The terms for the nine were identical across the board: the same fee, alphabetical credits, equal billing, no individual names on the poster, publishing for all. “Very, very, very little money,” he says.

By the time the agents started calling to ask what he was doing, he had two and a half composers signed on. By the time he was finished, composers were calling him.

Gilroy doesn’t want “Behemoth!” compared to Todd Field’s Cate Blanchett vehicle “Tár,” and he doesn’t want it described as a classical music movie, which he says makes the movie “start to sound like spinach.”

He would rather viewers hear it as a film about family and about what he calls the “new varieties of loneliness” in a fragmented world.

What breaks his heart, he says, is the phrase “too late.” He has been married 43 years, has a grandchild and is tight with his brothers and his team.

“I’m trying,” he says when asked — or, more accurately, begged — not to wait another 14 years before making another movie. “We’re going to make 30 movies a year, right?”

Searchlight Pictures will open “Behemoth!” in theaters on Dec. 4.

The conversation below has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Variety Awards Circuit: Oscars

I don’t know if it’s habituation or remembering the ancestral lands, but I was completely designed, self-designed over the years, for 128 pages and a two-hour experience. Six months of prep, six months of shooting, this 18-month agrarian system. It was a great system. I couldn’t imagine doing something long, and then I really wanted to do it. But showrunning was like super directing. It’s not so different.

I finally had the idea on “Rogue One” during the scoring sessions with Michael Giacchino. It was too exciting to be there. There had to be a movie there. After that, I spent six months interviewing musicians. One person would lead me to somebody else. There were musicians from “Rogue One” and “Michael Clayton,” people I’d gotten to know over the years. Movie journalism is really fun because people can lie to you and make stuff up, but you really do get an essential truth. People will tell you a lot.

I knew a lot, but I didn’t have a hook. Then I got swept away in “Andor.” After that long post on “Andor,” you have time to figure out what you want to do next. I wanted to get away from the anger, politics and noise of “Andor.” I was eager for a sanctuary, at least for a moment, to clear my head. So I worked extra hard to find that hook, and I got it.

Everybody gets up and goes, “Oh, it was amazing and fantastic.” I’m just going to be part of that Hollywood compliment train because I don’t have any other story to tell. The guy was immaculate from day one.

When Oscar left, there was a traffic jam between “Frankenstein” and awards and I tried to push again. I didn’t want to lose my people, but I didn’t want to push anymore. All of a sudden, Pedro was there. Sanne and I went out to lunch to meet him, and I was rehearsing in the car the speech I was going to give my people: “Hey, we really tried hard, but we’re not going to do this movie now. I’m going to try to come up with something else for us to do.” It’s hard to keep a team. So I was preparing the disappointing speech when we went into lunch.

10 minutes in, I’m like, “Oh my God, can he be this perfect? He must be. There must be something wrong with him. What’s wrong?” Brilliant actor, complete natural, all singing, all dancing. But he’s in every scene, in every moment and he doesn’t have a whole lot to say. I wanted the movie to have sparkle. I wanted to justify the exclamation point.

We had a three-hour meeting that was more of a prenup than a meeting because after about half an hour, we’d decided, “OK, we like you, you like us, nobody’s selling anything.” That’s how meetings should be. We said, “This is everything we would need” and he said, “This is what I would need.” Then he said, “I’ll start tomorrow.” The next day, he had a cello.

Forty-plus days. Our prep was five, six months. This was a prep movie, huge prep. It’s a lot of movie for not a lot of money, so you’ve got to be very prepped.

It’s a movie about a cellist. Good luck. Takes place in fractured time. I’m probably going to need nine composers. And, oh, by the way, there’s no scenario where we can go to Atlanta or Australia. We’re making a movie about a disappearing coral reef. It would violate the whole battle of the movie. We need to employ 303 union musicians, and we’ve got to shoot in L.A. We’ve got to pay all the fringes. The fringes on this movie probably cost what “Nightcrawler” cost. So that’s a tough one.

The pitch was fun. “Hey, I’m making a movie about your world. You want to read the script? I’m doing this really daffy thing.” With the first couple of people, it was, “If you don’t like it or you’re not interested, it’s a cutout. If you do, we’ll get involved with the agents later, because there’s no money here. But please read it before you call.”

I knew I had James Newton Howard because I had the closest relationship with him over the years. I thought he would do the final piece, so I had an anchor there. James will kill the “Behemoth” part at the end.

Henry Jackman was the first one in. Our music supervisor, who’s the unsung hero in a lot of this, said, “I think Henry would be really into this.” We met very quickly, and he was in right away. Then he started connecting me to people. I had two and a half composers before the agents started calling: “What the fuck are you doing? Why are you calling my client?”

The deal was always the same. I’m not going to have anybody play against type. What’s the point of that? Everybody gets the same fee, no matter who you are. Some people had much more work than others, but everybody gets the same. The credits will always be under the Behemoth Collective, always alphabetical, always equal billing. On posters, we only put the collective. We will not put individual names. We got everybody their publishing, which I’m not sure how precedent-setting that was, but it seemed to be really unusual. Very, very, very little money. Everybody had approval over the mixes. Those were the ground rules.

When I finished, a couple of people wanted to get in and I had no more room.

Searchlight has a featurette they’re going to do, and the soundtrack goes up on Spotify. They’re going to do a big push on it. But I don’t know how you would do that in the movie.

It’s absolutely on the page. I don’t know what Variety’s position on the movie gods is, but it’s the religion I subscribe to and the movie gods really smiled on me with the casting. I get Pedro. Then I had a couple of women I instinctively thought I’d go to first, but people weren’t available or it wasn’t working. Then Olivia’s name came up, and I’m like, oh my God, why didn’t we start there? What’s she going to say? I think I heard from her within 12 hours.

I’ve directed a lot of directors. There’s something really super clean about directing a director, particularly someone that intelligent. I said, “I’ll answer any question you want. Carol doesn’t lose any arguments. She declares victory and walks away. I’ll tell you anything else.” She goes, “No, I got it.”

Her scenes are Exhibit A for why you don’t rehearse. I’ll rehearse if something’s complicated or new, but by and large, I want to watch not just Pedro but the crew when that shit flows on screen. Not a lot of takes. She comes in and stands and delivers.

If you say it’s about music and cellos, and I hate using the term classical music because it’s mostly movie music, it starts to sound like spinach. It starts to sound starchy, like this movie is going to be good for you. But this is really about family and family history, and about how there are so many new varieties of loneliness in the world. Loneliness used to be reserved for a couple of categories. Now there are many ways to be lonely, and as society gets fragmented, people get lonelier.

I also think the term midlife crisis was a good term for people to get their heads around the fact that people have crises in their lives, but the timing isn’t accurate. We have all kinds of moments, and they come at different times. There’s a decisive thing where something’s just not right, some unexpected quest, something incomplete that has to be taken care of or not taken care of or run away from. We all have that. So I think it’s a super universal family film, in terms of family dynamics and family drama, with a very emotional, hopefully cathartic ending.

This is a movie where the character is working the same puzzle you are. Why are we going here? Why are we going back 20 years? He has a question as big as anything at the end, and you become a collaborator with him on it. That’s an unusual movie to make.

I don’t like when we’re compared to “Tár.” And I don’t love that comparison because I don’t think Pedro’s character is a womanizer.

When you play music, you have this outlet that automatically puts you into a community and New York is just a family. But man, when you pack up your case and go home, there you are. For Alex, the demands placed on him as a child, the shape-shifting he had to do to stay in the zone and his nomadic existence make it easy for him to slip into giving everybody what they want. You never give people what they need, but you can give everybody what they want. That combination may look really interesting and chic to somebody on the outside, but man.

The exclamation point is there for a reason. When Pedro came on, there were a lot of things I wanted to say to the crew and the department heads about the kind of movie I wanted to make that I’d been nervous about. Pedro gave me permission, with his effervescence and his sadness and his ability to mask his sadness, to go after the fairy tale. A fairy-tale underpinning underpins this. He’s a minstrel with a thorn in his foot. If he doesn’t pull the thorn out, he’ll walk in circles for the rest of his life. This is a guy who’s finding that thorn and, hopefully, pulling it by the end. All the oxygen of the movie, all the things that are his sanctuary and, in a way, his prison, is movie music.

I really wanted to be a musician. I started gigging when I was 12. I went to Boston to play music. By my second year, at 18, I dropped out and joined a band. Boston was a great place in the ’70s for playing original music.

My father was around movies my whole life, so I understood how movies were made. Still, none of the three of us had aspirations to go into the movie business. Our father moved us so we wouldn’t. But Boston was a great movie town. There were three rep houses. Everybody could see everything all the time. I’d go to a double feature every day and play at night. For about 15 years, I saw everything.

I read the same things you read. I listen to the same things you listen to. I have all your anxieties. My only trick is that I never take a job in front of the one I’m on. It’s like popping your head out of a hole. What’s going on? Where’s the shrapnel coming from? What’s clear ground? Where do people want something? Then I try to find a place where something that interests me intersects with the possibility of production, without being tied down. I don’t have a company. I don’t have employees. I don’t have seven scripts backed up in a studio that’s constipated or no longer exists.

I’ve written more things that haven’t gotten made than have ever gotten made. My office is full of them.

They vary in value over time. Some things are too close because you wrote them in a moment, and it’s not a distant moment yet. Then enough time goes by, and they become a period piece. Some things, the issue has disappeared. Some things were extremely hip or important at the moment, and that’s gone. I’m in the sifting-through-the-compost-pile mode right now. I’ve got a couple of things.

No. I’ve been married to the same woman for 43 years. I have a grandchild. I’m really tight with my brothers. I have a team of people who are really close and love working together. I feel very, very, very connected.

But as I’ve gotten older, as you lose your energy a little bit, what rises? My level of empathy is just overdamped. Coming off “Andor,” I realized the power of empathy. If I let my emotions walk free for every character, I can take them to another level. What breaks my heart more than anything else is “too late.” To me, “too late” is the thing. Oh, man, you missed it. You missed your chance to connect. You missed your chance to say that. It breaks me. “Michael Clayton” is too late, right? There are so many ways to pretend you’re not lonely now that are just enhancing it, all the fragmentation we have. That’s not a new idea. But I don’t see many people dealing with it, and I put him in that category.

People will ask, “Why Pedro?” Pedro gives me the total party. He’s a host, and he’s lively, charming, fast and quick. But he gives me all the regret and all the fear as well. It’s all underneath there, legitimately. He doesn’t have to travel very far to get to it.

News

Souraya Noujaim Appointed as Director of the Louvre Abu Dhabi

SOURAYA NOUJAIM . Courtesy the Louvre Abu Dhabi.

Abu Dhabi’s Department of Culture and Tourism has announced Lebanese art historian and curator Souraya Noujaim as the new director of the Louvre Abu Dhabi. She succeeds founding director Manuel Rabaté, who departed from the institution earlier this year to helm the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art in New Delhi.

Born in Beirut, Noujaim brings several decades’ worth of scholarly and leadership experience to the role. With a PhD in Islamic art history and archaeology from Paris Nanterre University, she previously headed the Department of Islamic Arts and the French Grand Department of Islamic Art Heritage at the Louvre in Paris. There, she oversaw more than 18,000 Islamic artworks, and curated several traveling exhibitions, including “From the Louvre: Masterpieces of Islamic Art” (2026) at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Asian Art, and “Mamluks: Legacy of an Empire” (2025) at the Louvre Abu Dhabi.

Noujaim’s appointment marks a return to the Louvre Abu Dhabi, where she served as the inaugural scientific, curatorial, and collections management director from 2018 to 2023, helping to shape the museum’s vision and collection. “Louvre Abu Dhabi holds a special place in my professional and personal journey,” Noujaim said in a press release. “I look forward to working with our teams, partners, and communities to build on this legacy, deepen our engagement with audiences, expand and enrich our collection, and explore new ways of making art and culture accessible, relevant, and inspiring for all.”

Harison Butler is an editorial intern at ArtAsiaPacific.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Pierson Fodé has signed with Range Media Partners for representation.

He will next be seen in the Netflix thriller The Last Mrs. Parrish , opposite Jennifer Lopez, Isabel May, and Nikolaj Coster-Waldau. Directed by Academy Award winner Robert Zemeckis, the film, which has wrapped production, is based on the 2017 national and international bestseller of the same name by Liv Constantine, the pen name of sisters Lynne and Valerie Constantine.

Fodé is coming off two hit romantic comedies starting with Netflix’s romantic comedy The Wrong Paris opposite Miranda Cosgrove, which quickly shot to the #1 spot on Netflix. He also had Hulu’s Swiped alongside Lily James, who played Bumble founder Whitney Wolfe Herd in the biographical drama, which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival. It reached Hulu’s #1 spot internationally.

Related Stories

Zac Efron Signs With Range Media Partners

'Lioness' Actor Dave Annable Signs With Range Media Partners

He then capped oﬀ the year with Steve Carr’s holiday comedy A Merry Little Ex-Mas with Alicia Silverstone, Oliver Hudson, and Jameela Jamil, which debuted as the #2 most-watched English-language movie globally on Netflix.

Watch on Deadline

Fodé’s breakout film role came in The Man From Toronto from Patrick Hughes, opposite Kevin Hart and Woody Harrelson, which also rose to #1 on Netflix; while earlier this year, he was back on the festival circuit with the edgy romantic thriller Dope Queens , which premiered at the Palm Springs International Film Festival.

He continues to be represented by CAA; Gang, Tyre, Ramer, Brown & Passman; and The Initiative Group.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 他在新美术馆的回顾展为我们理解文化转变提供了一个契机。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Arthur Jafa如今已是大红大紫的明星，大多数艺术爱好者都对他的故事耳熟能详。但过去并非总是如此。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "直到大约十年前，他基本上还是一位“艺术家心中的艺术家”，游走于电影界和艺术界之间。他的声誉直到2016年在其50岁出头时才彻底爆发，当时正值唐纳德·J·特朗普令人震惊地击败希拉里·克林顿之后不久。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他的视频作品《Love Is the Message, The Message Is Death》（2016年）在大选后的几天里吸引了无数观众前往哈莱姆区的Gavin Brown’s Enterprise画廊，并引发了参观者和评论家的强烈情感反应。自那以后，Jafa一直被奉为智者，荣誉纷至沓来。由新美术馆馆长Massimiliano Gioni和资深策展人Gary Carrion-Murayari共同策划的新美术馆近期举办的他的作品回顾展，只是最新的一例。", "links": [{"text": "critics", "url": "https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2017/01/23/arthur-jafas-crucial-ode-to-black-america"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Gavin Brown的故事已经被讲过太多次，几乎不值得重提。我提到这一点是为了强调，围绕Jafa的讨论一直是由一个非常特殊的文化时刻塑造的：2016年之后的清算与抵抗时期，即作家Molly Fischer所说的“流行文化的伟大觉醒期”。现在有些人称之为“觉醒1.0版”。", "links": [{"text": "Pop Culture’s Great Awokening", "url": "https://www.thecut.com/2018/01/pop-cultures-great-awokening.html"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://news.artnet.com/app/news-upload/2026/10/arthur_jafa_I_am_tony_install_shot_processed-1024x768.jpg", "alt": "画廊角落并置了一尊青铜躯干雕塑、一个出拳击打岩石的漫画绿巨人剪纸，以及一幅写着“新黑人无所畏惧”（“The New Negro Has No Fear”）的复古照片壁画。", "caption": "", "credit": "Artnet News", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "新美术馆“Arthur Jafa: I Am Tony”展厅现场。摄影：Ben Davis。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个词最近由亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯（Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez）推广开来。这位民主党女议员收回了她之前的一些言论，暗示了进步派政治家之间的一种新共识：“觉醒1.0版太疯狂了。”", "links": [{"text": "popularized", "url": "https://theweek.com/politics/democrats-progressives-wrestle-woke-era"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "社会正义已经过时了吗？还是说只是转向了更务实的东西？文化是正在走向后觉醒、反觉醒、“黑暗觉醒”，还是正在进入某种觉醒2.0时代？安娜·康布卢（Anna Kornbluh）的《Immediacy》、奥卢费米·O·泰沃（Olúfẹ́mi O. Táíwò）的《Elite Capture》、凯瑟琳·刘（Catherine Liu）的《Traumatized》以及安东·耶格尔（Anton Jäger）的《Hyperpolitics》都是近期出版的文化理论著作，它们敏锐度各不相同，试图表达这样一个观点：2016年之后的自由派象征政治具有还原论色彩且极具破坏性。（我的上一本书《Art in the
